title: Pro-étale cohomology of a pro-étale affine
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $\Lambda$ a ring, $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{ét}},\Lambda)$, and let
$U=\varprojlim_{i\in I}U_i$ be a pro-étale affine over $X$, the limit being
cofiltered with affine transition maps and each $U_i$ affine and étale over
$X$. Write $K_i=K|_{U_i}\in D^+((U_i)_{\mathrm{ét}},\Lambda)$ and $K_U$ for the
inverse image of $K$ on $U_{\mathrm{ét}}$. Then for every $n\in\mathbf Z$ the
canonical maps

$$
\varinjlim_iH^n((U_i)_{\mathrm{ét}},K_i)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
H^n(U_{\mathrm{ét}},K_U)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
H^n(U_{\mathrm{proét}},(\nu_X^*K)|_U)
$$

are isomorphisms; equivalently
$R\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{proét}},(\nu_X^*K)|_U)\simeq\varinjlim_iR\Gamma((U_i)_{\mathrm{ét}},K_i)$
as a filtered derived colimit.

Here rings have a unit and modules are left modules. The coefficient ring sheaf on either site is the sheafification of the constant presheaf of rings with value $\Lambda$; $D^+$ is the bounded-below derived category of its module sheaves. The functor $\nu_X^*$ applies the geometric inverse image to the underlying sheaf and its addition and scalar action; this is exact. Cohomology means right-derived sections at the terminal object, in $\Lambda$-modules. The presentation index is small and nonempty, and the colimits are indexed by $I^{\mathrm{op}}$, in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. The filtered derived colimit is formed from any bounded-below complex $I^\bullet$ of injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions] $\Lambda$-module sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$ representing $K$: the section complexes $I^\bullet(U_i)$, with the sheaf restriction maps along the transitions $U_j\to U_i$, form a strict $I^{\mathrm{op}}$-diagram of complexes of $\Lambda$-modules, each $I^\bullet(U_i)$ computes $R\Gamma((U_i)_{\mathrm{ét}},K_i)$, and $\varinjlim_iR\Gamma((U_i)_{\mathrm{ét}},K_i)$ denotes the degreewise colimit of this diagram, which is also its left-derived colimit. The asserted isomorphism in $D^+(\Lambda\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})$ induces on $H^n$ the composite of the two displayed maps.

proof.text: *Step 1: coefficients and forgetting scalars.* Work with left modules over the constant ring sheaf on each small site. By [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image], every inverse image used below is exact, retains the underlying abelian inverse image, and preserves constant coefficients, including for noncommutative $\Lambda$. By [lem-pe-left-module-derived-evaluation-forget], derived evaluation of any bounded-below module complex agrees with abelian derived evaluation after forgetting scalars, compatibly with section pullbacks. Thus the abelian comparison and continuity theorems below give the desired module cohomology maps, with their scalar actions. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] and [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] bounded-below injective module representatives exist. Abelian sheaves are modules over the constant integer sheaf, with the unique integer action given by repeated addition; the same Grothendieck assertion applies to them when using the complex acyclicity criterion.

proof.text:
*Step 2: restriction to $U$.* The presentation in the statement is exactly the small-cofiltered $X$-scheme presentation in clause 1 of [det-pe-classical-definition-continuity-map], with arrows $a:j	o i$, transitions $u_a:U_j	o U_i$, and projections $u_i:U	o U_i$. That clause supplies $U$ and the $U_i$ as site objects and the transitions and projections as site arrows. Only this geometric clause is used: its optional commutative coefficient ring may be chosen as $\mathbf Z$, independently of our arbitrary $\Lambda$. No module-classicality assertion and no affine-base ind-étale identification from that node is used. Apply the site assertion (1) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] (with the auxiliary ring there chosen as $\mathbf Z$) to identify $U_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with $X_{\mathrm{proét}}/U$. On an object $V	o U$, [lem-cbc-comparison-pullback-sections] identifies the underlying sheaf of $(
u_X^*F)|_U$ with $\Gamma(V_{\mathrm{ét}},(V	o X)^{-1}F)$. The same statement applied on $U$ identifies $
u_U^*(u_{\mathrm{ét}}^{-1}F)$ there with $\Gamma(V_{\mathrm{ét}},(V	o U)^{-1}u_{\mathrm{ét}}^{-1}F)$. The composition isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] identifies these expressions, compatibly with restrictions. Naturality with addition and every scalar endomorphism makes the identification $\Lambda$-linear. Restriction is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-restriction-exact], and inverse images are exact by step 1, so applying these sheaf isomorphisms degreewise gives the canonical derived identification $(
u_X^*K)|_U\cong
u_U^*K_U$.

*Step 3: global-sections comparison without a coefficient restriction.* Choose a bounded-below complex $J$ of injective $\Lambda_U$-module sheaves representing $K_U$, using step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. For every $J^m$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison] gives $H^p(U_{\mathrm{ét}},J^m_{ab})=0$ for $p>0$. Apply [lem-cbc-abelian-etale-proetale-cohomology-comparison] to $J^m_{ab}$: the underlying abelian sheaf of $
u_U^*J^m$ is sections-acyclic on $U_{\mathrm{proét}}$, and the canonical degree-zero map $\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{ét}},J^m)	o\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{proét}},
u_U^*J^m)$ is an isomorphism. The evaluation comparison on the pro-étale site makes $
u_U^*J^m$ sections-acyclic in module sheaves as well. By step 1, using [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact], $
u_U^*J$ represents $
u_U^*K_U$. Thus the complex acyclic-resolution criterion [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] makes $\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{proét}},
u_U^*J)$ a model for its module derived sections. The degree-zero section comparisons commute with the differentials, since section pullback is natural, and are $\Lambda$-linear by construction. They give an isomorphism of $\Lambda$-module complexes from $\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{ét}},J)$ to this pro-étale section complex. This proves the canonical derived comparison in $D^+(\Lambda	ext{-}\mathrm{Mod})$, and step 2 identifies its target with the one in the statement. Taking cohomology proves the second displayed arrow for every integer $n$.

proof.text: *Step 4: continuity.* Each $U_i$ is an affine object of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$, hence is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-qcqs-finite-family-geometry]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-etale-cohomology-limit] with $T=X$, $Y_i=U_i$, $Y=U$, and the underlying abelian complex of $K$. Its hypotheses are precisely the small cofiltered presentation, affine transition maps, qcqs stages, and bounded-below complex pulled back from $X$. Its stage objects are the inverse images along the étale maps $u_i:U_i\to X$; [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-restriction] identifies each of them with the restriction $K|_{U_i}=K_i$ of the statement, naturally and with the inverse-image unit on sections equal to restriction of sections, and the module structures agree because the identification is natural in the addition and scalar endomorphisms. It therefore gives the first displayed canonical map as an isomorphism in every integer degree. By step 1 it computes module cohomology as well. All transition and comparison maps commute with the scalar endomorphisms of $K$, so these are isomorphisms of $\Lambda$-modules. This continuity statement uses the entire given index category; no unproved change from the presentation to a stage overcategory is made.

proof.text: *Step 5: the stage complexes and their actual transition maps.* Choose the bounded-below injective representative $I^\bullet$ of $K$ from step 1. Apply [lem-pe-injective-complex-slice-section-model] on $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$. For every $i$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open] identifies $X_{\mathrm{ét}}/U_i$ with $(U_i)_{\mathrm{ét}}$, with identical coverings and sectionwise restriction. By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-restriction] the geometric inverse image along the étale map $U_i\to X$ is naturally isomorphic to this restriction, with the unit on sections equal to restriction of sections; naturality in addition and scalar endomorphisms makes it a module isomorphism. Therefore the new slice-model lemma identifies $C_i^\bullet=I^\bullet(U_i)$ with $R\Gamma((U_i)_{\mathrm{ét}},K_i)$ and identifies its literal restriction maps with the canonical derived transition maps. Its strict-diagram clause gives a strict $I^{\mathrm{op}}$-diagram with a common lower bound. For each injective term $I^m$, its restriction to every stage is sections-acyclic.

source.place: Blueprint Steps 3–4; repair of existing split Step 5, first paragraph; Stacks 03F3

proof.text: *Step 6: acyclic terms at the limit and the colimit complex.* Let $u:U\to X$. Apply step 4 to $I^m[0]$, for each integer $m$. By step 5 and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison] the positive abelian stage cohomology of its underlying sheaf vanishes. Hence $H^q(U_{\mathrm{ét}},u^*I^m)=0$ for every $q>0$, while the degree-zero continuity map is $\varinjlim_i I^m(U_i)\cong\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{ét}},u^*I^m)$. Naturality of section pullback makes these degreewise isomorphisms commute with the differential, so they give an isomorphism of complexes $\varinjlim_i C_i^\bullet\cong\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{ét}},u^*I^\bullet)$. Exactness from [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] says that $u^*I^\bullet$ represents $K_U$. Its terms are sections-acyclic in module sheaves by the preceding vanishing and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison], so [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] (3) identifies this section complex with $R\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{ét}},K_U)$. The hypothesis that the module category is Grothendieck is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck]. The comparison maps here are the actual section pullbacks from the fixed model.

source.place: Blueprint Steps 3–4; repair of existing split Step 5, second paragraph

proof.text: *Step 7: filtered derived colimit and conclusion.* Filtered colimits of abelian groups are exact by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact]. For left $\Lambda$-modules the colimit has representatives $[i,x]$, with addition formed at a common later stage and scalar action $r[i,x]=[i,rx]$; the equality relation is eventual equality. Thus its underlying abelian group is the abelian-group filtered colimit, and it is exact as well. Applying exactness to the kernel, image and quotient sequences defining cohomology gives $H^n(\varinjlim_i C_i)=\varinjlim_i H^n(C_i)$, for every $n\in\mathbf Z$. In particular degreewise filtered colimit carries objectwise quasi-isomorphisms of strict diagrams of complexes to quasi-isomorphisms. Therefore degreewise colimit on the category of strict $I^{\mathrm{op}}$-diagrams of complexes already sends the weak equivalences (objectwise quasi-isomorphisms) to quasi-isomorphisms. Its left-derived functor on that diagram category is computed by the same degreewise colimit: replacing a diagram by a quasi-isomorphic resolution does not change the result. The diagram of the statement is exactly the strict diagram $C_i^\bullet=I^\bullet(U_i)$ of steps 5–6, so its degreewise colimit is also its left-derived colimit, and steps 5–6 shows that each $C_i^\bullet$ computes $R\Gamma((U_i)_{\mathrm{ét}},K_i)$. Steps 5–6 therefore identifies the filtered derived colimit with $R\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{ét}},K_U)$; composing with step 3 gives the stated pro-étale derived isomorphism. Its cohomology maps are exactly the two displayed restriction maps, because the complexes and cocone maps in steps 5–6 are the section pullbacks themselves. This also explains the equivalence of the cohomological and derived formulations in the statement.

lean.statement: theorem proEtaleAffineContinuity {I : Type u} [SmallCategory I] [IsCofiltered I] (X : Scheme.{u}) (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [Ring Λ] (D : I ⥤ X.Etale) (c : Cone (D ⋙ Scheme.toProEt X)) (hc : IsLimit ((Scheme.ProEt.forget X ⋙ Over.forget X).mapCone c)) [∀ i : I, IsAffine (D.obj i).left] [∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map f).left] (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))) (L : CochainComplex (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) ℤ) (a : ℤ) [L.IsStrictlyGE a] [∀ n : ℤ, Injective (L.X n)] (e : DerivedCategory.Q.obj L ≅ K.obj) : IsIso (affineContinuityEtaleMap D c K.obj L e) ∧ IsIso (affineContinuityProEtaleMap D c K.obj L e) ∧ ∀ i : I, IsIso (DerivedCategory.Q.map (affineContinuityStageRestriction (D.obj i) L) ≫ affineContinuityTargetComparison (Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) (D.obj i).hom) (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 (D.obj i).left)) K.obj L e)
lean.note: Uses the existing fixed-coefficient Sheaf (ModuleCat Λ) encoding and unrestricted upstream comparison inverse image; no finiteness or commutativity restriction. The maps are built from the strict diagram of section complexes of any bounded-below injective representative, adjunction units, sheaf restrictions, and derived evaluation units. Invertibility of the two arrows with common colimit source is the canonical two-arrow assertion; the second displayed arrow is uniquely determined by their factorization. The final clause records that each stage complex computes its specified derived sections.
